# Delivery Gates Checklist: Orca Documentation Truth Pass

**Purpose**: Validate that the requirements for the Orca documentation correction are complete, clear, consistent, and measurable before delivery.
**Created**: 2026-11-17
**Feature**: [spec.md](spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on the feature context and the delivery focus: claim accuracy, retained macOS facts, no behavior change, and style.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact.
Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality.
It does not mean implementation work is complete.
**Defaults used**: standard depth, pull-request reviewer audience, focus on the claim-accuracy and no-behavior-change clusters, because the request named no further scope and no interaction was possible.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Is a requirement stated for each of the six stale statements, so that none of them depends on an unstated edit? [Completeness, Spec §FR-001, §FR-003, §FR-004, §FR-005, §FR-006, §FR-007]
- [ ] CHK002 Is each of the captain's three decisions stated as its own requirement with the document that must carry it? [Completeness, Spec §FR-009, §FR-010, §FR-011]
- [ ] CHK003 Is the content of the new Linux verification entry enumerated field by field, so that an entry missing one field is detectably incomplete? [Completeness, Spec §FR-015]
- [ ] CHK004 Is the recovery-skill requirement stated for placement and for the exact amount of change, not only for its meaning? [Completeness, Spec §FR-017]
- [ ] CHK005 Are requirements defined for the Orca claims that sit in files the feature must not touch, so a reader knows they remain a known follow-up? [Gap, Spec §FR-021, §Assumptions]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK006 Is "qualify the macOS facts rather than deleting them" defined by an observable condition, such as a label on each retained sentence? [Clarity, Spec §FR-001, §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK007 Is "not exercised live" distinguished from "verified" for each claim whose only source is help text or a server bundle? [Clarity, Spec §FR-005, §FR-016]
- [ ] CHK008 Is "cannot host Orca work" for a folder-registered project stated with the reason and with what the spawn path does today, so it does not read as a guarantee the code enforces? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-010]
- [ ] CHK009 Is "refused with an Orca-hosted primary" for away and quiet modes tied to an observable refusal and not only to intent? [Clarity, Spec §FR-011]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK010 Do the requirement that the Orca capability matrix row stays unchanged and the requirement to stop attributing the missing keys to Orca's API agree with each other? [Consistency, Spec §FR-012, §FR-013]
- [ ] CHK011 Does the requirement to leave the adapter's own header comment unchanged agree with the requirement that no document claim Orca lacks a key primitive? [Conflict, Spec §FR-005, §FR-021]
- [ ] CHK012 Do the "no behavior change" requirement and the permitted inventory edit describe the same permitted set of non-prose changes? [Consistency, Spec §FR-018]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK013 Can SC-001 be judged from the finished files by an observable check for each of the six statements? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001]
- [ ] CHK014 Can SC-002 be judged by a reader who has not seen the evaluation report, and are its seven questions listed in the story? [Measurability, Spec §SC-002, §US1]
- [ ] CHK015 Is each acceptance scenario traceable to a behavior and a check through the test list? [Traceability, Spec §User Scenarios]
- [ ] CHK016 Is SC-005, the re-read against the evidence, defined by an artifact a reviewer can open rather than by an assertion that it was done? [Measurability, Spec §SC-005, §FR-020]

## Scope and Boundaries

- [ ] CHK017 Are the install hint, startup-terminal adoption, folder-kind refusal, and leftover-branch behavior recorded as out of scope with a reason? [Boundary, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK018 Is it stated why the Linux `PATH` prerequisite is in scope although CLI discovery is another slice? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions, Research R4]

## Dependencies and Assumptions

- [ ] CHK019 Is the assumption that the evaluation report's observations still hold on the evaluated host marked as confirmed by named read-only commands where it was confirmed, and as unconfirmed elsewhere? [Assumption, Research R1]
- [ ] CHK020 Is the dependency on firstmate's own documentation audience inventory stated, including that every new tracked document needs a classification? [Dependency, Spec §FR-018]
- [ ] CHK021 Is the unfilled project constitution recorded as a limitation on the TDD principle and not silently ignored? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions]

## Notes

Reviewers own checklist markers; `/speckit-implement` reads checklist state and does not modify markers.
Items CHK001 to CHK021 are open for the reviewer; the delivery pipeline's review and the operator are the intended reviewers.
